record.hypothesis: Two 128×96 RGB images were serialized as three channel-major planes, giving 36,864 carrier samples each. The integer packing is int16 = (uint8 - 128) × 128, encoded as mono 48 kHz FLAC. The native decoded PCM matches exactly. Chromium decodeAudioData at 48 kHz produces floats that are not exact multiples of the ideal scale in every case. Nearest-grid recovery, round(sample × 256 + 128), recovers every original byte. The maximum pre-rounding value error is below 0.0039, safely below half a data level on these fixtures. The earlier raw-float equality check was intentionally retained in browser_initial.json; the final claim is reversible integer recovery, not bit-identical floating-point PCM. At a 44.1 kHz context rate, resampling changes both count (36,864→33,868) and values, and the carrier is rejected. Context-rate resampling is part of the documented decoding contract [S6]. No carrier signal is connected to speakers.
